checks.message: Alarm has no actions configured — it will fire silently
checks.context: An alarm without actions just changes state in the console. Nobody gets notified, no auto-remediation runs. Wire it to an SNS topic at minimum so someone actually knows when it triggers.

checks.message: Deleting alarms removes monitoring coverage — verify nothing critical depends on them
checks.context: If these alarms were triggering auto-scaling, auto-remediation, or on-call notifications, deleting them silently removes that coverage. Document what each alarm does before removing it.

checks.message: Verify the dashboard doesn't expose sensitive metric dimensions publicly
checks.context: CloudWatch dashboards can be shared publicly via a shareable link. If you later enable public sharing, any metric dimensions (account IDs, resource names, IP addresses) become visible to anyone with the link.

checks.message: Contributor Insights rules incur per-event charges — scope the rule to avoid unexpected costs
checks.context: Rules that match high-volume log groups (e.g. VPC flow logs, ALB access logs) can generate millions of events per hour. Scope the rule with a specific log group and filter pattern.

checks.message: Manually setting alarm state can suppress real alerts
checks.context: Setting an alarm to OK manually while the underlying condition is still breached will suppress notifications until the next evaluation cycle. Only use this for testing — never to silence a real alert.

checks.message: Disabling alarm actions stops all auto-remediation and notifications
checks.context: This is a common attacker technique after gaining access — disable alarms so that subsequent malicious activity doesn't trigger alerts. Ensure this is intentional and re-enable actions as soon as possible.
